answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by tying influence to a costly, non-transferable work record rather than to account count. Like tending a garden, trust grows only from completed, publicly checkable jobs over time, so a newcomer starts with tiny limits. Established peers, acting as falcon watchers, audit samples of that work, while a raven-like reputation graph flags identities whose endorsers overlap suspiciously. Creating thousands of fake agents then costs real compute, time and forfeited deposits, while one honest agent keeps its full standing.
